pillars.title: Ledger Service: Vendor Sync, Payments API, Event Ledger
pillars.objective: Implement ledgerd: a Python 3 standard-library-only service that syncs payments from the Meridian API v3 (paginated walk, retries, conditional requests), serves a RESTful payments/summary/buckets API, maintains an append-only event ledger with contiguous seq numbers, handles vendor webhooks (signature verification, idempotent application, transaction group atomicity), and hosts the frontend static files. Must boot within 10s, serve reads during sync, handle crashes/restarts cleanly.
research_questions: How to implement the 192-page paginated vendor walk with Resume-after-dropped-connection, Retry-After handling, and cursor-expired restart using only Python stdlib?
How to implement the conditional sync generation rule (304 with mismatched X-Collection-Generation triggers exactly one unconditional refetch)?
How to implement idempotent webhook application with version-order enforcement and transaction-group atomicity (stage parts, apply in one local transaction)?
How to ensure the event ledger maintains strictly increasing contiguous seq from 1 across crashes and restarts?
How to serve reads (payments, summary, buckets, viz records) within latency budgets while a sync is in flight using stdlib threading?
acceptance_criteria: Service binds 127.0.0.1 and is listening within 10 seconds of process start
Full 192-page sync walk completes within 120 seconds including documented waits
GET /api/payments?limit=50 responds in under 150ms p95 including during sync with 8 concurrent readers
GET /api/buckets responds in under 200ms p95; GET /api/summary under 150ms p95
GET /api/viz/records responds in under 400ms p95
Event ledger seq is strictly increasing and contiguous from 1 with no gaps
Webhook endpoint answers within 3 seconds, verifies signatures against raw body, applies events idempotently
Transaction groups (refund + reversal) are applied atomically - no read observes half-applied group
Restart against existing --db-dir resumes cleanly: idempotent schema init, no data loss, no duplicate application
Vendor unreachable at boot: binds anyway, serves local data, shows degraded state, retries sync no less often than every 5 seconds
Every vendor request has timeout of at most 10 seconds
exclusions: Maker/checker approval workflow and drafts API
Outbox pattern, relay to notifierd, notification materialization
Frontend HTML/CSS/JS console page and 3D visualization

pillars.title: Approval Workflow, Outbox Relay, and Notifier Service
pillars.objective: Implement the maker/checker approval workflow (draft state machine, four-eyes rule, idempotent vendor send), the outbox pattern with background relay to notifierd (at-least-once delivery, batch size ≤50, backoff capped at 2s), and notifierd service (idempotent event consumer by seq, selective notification materialization for 4 event types). Must survive SIGKILL at any point with state intact and no doubled vendor payments.
research_questions: How to implement the draft state machine (draft → submitted → approved|rejected, approved → sent) with four-eyes rule (approver ≠ submitter)?
How to implement the idempotent vendor send with stored Idempotency-Key that survives crashes and ensures exactly one vendor payment per approved draft?
How to implement the outbox pattern where rows commit in the same SQLite transaction as the state change they announce?
How to implement the background relay that delivers outbox rows in batches of ≤50 ascending seq with backoff capped at 2s, marking delivered only after 200?
How to implement notifierd's idempotent consumption by seq where duplicates never abort the batch?
acceptance_criteria: Draft state machine: draft → submitted → approved|rejected, approved → sent once vendor accepts
Four-eyes rule: approve/reject with same token that submitted returns 403 approval_forbidden
Idempotent vendor send: stored Idempotency-Key reused on retry, exactly one vendor payment per approved draft
Outbox rows commit in same SQLite transaction as the state change they announce
Background relay delivers outbox rows in batches of ≤50 ascending seq, backoff capped at 2s
User writes never block on notifier availability; while down, pending grows and relay catches up after heal
After ledgerd restart, relay resumes from durable outbox rows; nothing lost, nothing doubled
notifierd idempotent by seq: duplicate seq reported in 'duplicate', state untouched; mixed new/duplicate batches apply new and report each correctly
Selective materialization: exactly 4 event types produce notification rows (draft.submitted, draft.approved, draft.rejected, reversal.created); payment.sent processed but no notification
SIGKILL after submit's 200 or approve's 200 (mid-send): restart finds state intact, finishes send with same key
exclusions: Vendor sync and payments API (ledgerd core)
Frontend HTML/CSS/JS console page and 3D visualization

pillars.title: Operations Console: Payments Table, 3D Field Visualization, and Workflow UI
pillars.objective: Implement the single-page operations console (4 files: index.html, styles.css, app.js, viz.js totaling ≤150KB uncompressed) with payments table (server-driven pagination, filters, sorting, optimistic notes), interactive 3D field (raw WebGL, 12,288 instanced columns, GPU picking, inertial camera with closed-form coasting, collision-culled labels), notifications feed (poll ≤5s, degraded recovery within 5s), and drafts panel. Must work fully offline with zero external code.
research_questions: How to implement the 3D field with raw WebGL (no libraries) rendering 12,288 instanced columns within the draw budget of ≤8 default-FBO draws per frame?
How to implement GPU picking with an offscreen pick framebuffer, identity color encoding (idNum = n+1), and occlusion-correct decode?
How to implement the inertial camera with closed-form exponential decay (τ=0.4s) satisfying the remaining-coast identity and settle budget?
How to implement collision-culled screen-space labels that are occlusion-culled through the pick buffer?
How to implement demand rendering (0 default-FBO draws in any 500ms window at rest) while maintaining responsiveness?
acceptance_criteria: Four files (index.html, styles.css, app.js, viz.js) totaling ≤150KB uncompressed
First data rows render within 2 seconds of page load (local data present)
3D field shows first non-background frame within 3 seconds of page load at full count
Payments table uses server-driven pagination (limit/offset/status/currency/sort), never fetches whole collection
Custom dropdown filters with data-value attribute always reflecting current selection
Optimistic note editing: paints immediately before network responds, 409 reverts with non-blocking notice
Notifications feed polls ≤5 seconds, flips to degraded on 502, recovers within 5 seconds of heal without reload
Draw budget: ≤8 default-FBO draws per rendered frame; over 40-move drag window ≤384 total
Demand rendering: 0 default-FBO draws in any 500ms window at rest
GPU picking: pick buffer with identity color encoding, occlusion-correct, ≤4 offscreen draws per refresh
Camera: orbit with drag (yaw -0.30·Δx, pitch +0.30·Δy), wheel zoom (exp(0.0012·deltaY)), double-click reset
Inertia: closed-form exponential decay τ=0.4s, remaining-coast identity holds within tolerance
Labels: 12 highest-amount candidates, occlusion-culled through pick buffer, collision-culled, never overlap
Brush: linked between table and 3D field, dim non-members to 0.30, toggle on click
vs7dbg API: layout(), sceneDigest(), camera(), setCamera(), pick(), pickPixel(), brush(), frames() all synchronous and truthful
All timestamps rendered human-readable in user's locale, never raw ISO-8601 with offset
Money formatting: EUR/USD 2 decimals, JPY 0 decimals, KWD 3 decimals
exclusions: Ledger service vendor sync and payments API implementation
Approval workflow backend logic, outbox relay, notifierd service

integration_contract.objective: Verify that ledgerd and notifierd cooperate correctly: outbox events flow from ledgerd to notifierd, webhook handling integrates with the event ledger and payments API, frontend console correctly consumes all APIs (payments table, summary, buckets, 3D viz records, SSE stream, notifications proxy, drafts workflow), and the complete system survives the graded run's crash/restart scenarios while maintaining consistency.
interface_invariants: ledgerd serves frontend static files at GET / with correct content types
notifierd receives events via POST /notify/events from ledgerd's background relay
Frontend consumes GET /api/payments, /api/summary, /api/buckets, /api/viz/records, GET /api/stream (SSE), GET /api/notifications (proxied to notifierd), and POST /api/drafts* endpoints
Webhook endpoint at POST /api/webhooks/meridian receives vendor events and integrates with ledgerd's event processing
All API responses use the unified error envelope format
Cross-service communication flows over HTTP only - each service touches only its own database file
acceptance_criteria: Complete system boots with both services listening within 10 seconds

Full graded run completes: vendor down at boot, sync walk with dropped connection and Retry-After, webhooks racing the walk (out-of-order, duplicate, forged signature, mid-walk create, refund transaction group), conditional sync generation mismatch, ledgerd SIGKILL mid-sync and after draft submit/approve, notifierd SIGKILL with relay catch-up
At quiescence: every payment's version and status equals vendor's final committed state, row count matches vendor
No invented states: every applied (payment_id, version) exists in vendor's committed history
Per-key order maintained: applied versions per payment strictly increase in event-log order
Monotonic reads: version served for a payment never decreases between reads
Group atomicity: no read observes half-applied transaction group; per-currency reversal totals equal refunded payment amounts
Amount immutability: no served row shows different amount_minor than vendor-committed
Terminal conservation: per-currency counts and totals equal vendor ground truth including all app-created payments
No cross-currency sums in API, UI, or labels
Exactly-once effects: no doubled vendor payment, no doubled notification row, no ledger event applied twice downstream
Frontend console fully functional: payments table with pagination/filters/sorting, 3D field with all interactions, notifications feed with degraded recovery, drafts workflow end-to-end
